notes.text:
This is an ordinary unverified foundational audit for the restricted A–D assignment. Original P11 remains outside the claimed completion.

The imported premises are: existence of a smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed complementary form; Lamari's conversion of nonnegative pairings of a smooth real (1,1) form b against all such forms into b+dd^c q>=0 for a distribution q; unique canonical locally integrable psh representatives of distributions with positive complex Hessian; canonical radial convolution recovery; relative compactness of L1_loc-bounded psh families; coordinate invariance of geometric Lelong numbers; analyticity and dimension <=p of their positive upperlevel sets for CLOSED positive currents of bidimension (p,p); and local finiteness of global irreducible analytic components.

The primary sources are [Lamari, Courants kählériens et surfaces compactes, AIF 49 (1999)](https://www.numdam.org/article/AIF_1999__49_1_263_0.pdf), Proposition 1.3, printed 267–268, Lemma 3.3, printed 275–276, and the preceding duality on printed 267; and [Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf), I.4.17–4.20, I.5.8–5.9, III.7.2, III.8.5, and II.5.3. The author's [Books/documents page](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/documents.html) identifies the book and public PDF.

Lamari's primary PDF was successfully opened. Proposition 1.3, its separation argument, the duality context, and Lemma 3.3's printed separation proof were read. Screenshots of printed 275 and 276 confirm the nonnegative-pairing hypothesis, distribution conclusion, and absence of a d-closedness hypothesis on b. Our application has strictly positive pairings. A positive scalar difference in dd^c convention is absorbed by rescaling q.

Full CADG PDF opens timed out, and direct local downloads were denied by the network sandbox. Exact indexed passages from the author-hosted primary book were nevertheless retrieved: I.4.17–4.18, I.4.20 with canonical recovery, I.5.8 with its displayed proof and I.5.9's statement, III.7.2's coordinate-invariance argument, III.8.5's complete statement and short reduction to III.8.4, and II.5.3's global-component statement. III.7.2 is the location actually retrieved for coordinate invariance. We do not claim to have read the entire CADG PDF or recursively certified the permitted subharmonic compactness and Siu foundations.

Smooth perturbation invariance and the hyperplane Lelong normalization are reconstructed directly in n3. Siu is never applied to a nonclosed current.

notes.summary: A fixed Hermitian Hessian lower bound and sup_X u=0 give uniform global L1 bounds and canonical L1 compactness, with normalization retained. No closedness of omega is required.
notes.detailedSummary: Add nonnegative local quadratics to obtain psh functions. A submean inequality centered where u>=-E bounds the negative integral on an inner chart ball. Positive-volume overlaps propagate bounds along a finite connected cover from a point near the global supremum. Local psh compactness gives a compatible global L1 limit; canonical recovery glues the representatives pointwise. Moving-center submean inequalities at maximizers preserve supremum zero. This supplies A's normalization and compactness obligations.
notes.text:
Let X be connected and compact, omega a fixed smooth positive Hermitian form, lambda>0 fixed, and mu a smooth positive volume form. We prove uniform L1(mu) bounds and relative compactness for genuine quasi-psh u satisfying dd^c u>=-lambda omega and sup_X u=0. The canonical representative and local psh compactness premises are those audited in n1.

Choose finitely many coordinate balls W_i=B(0,4r_i), with closures inside coordinate domains, whose inner balls V_i=B(0,r_i) cover X. Choose rho_i=K_i|z_i|^2 so that dd^c rho_i>=lambda omega on W_i. Then p_i=u+rho_i is genuine psh. Fixed constants satisfy 0<=rho_i<=H_i and dmu<=M_i dLebesgue on W_i. The overlap graph of the V_i is connected, since otherwise their unions would disconnect X.

If x belongs to V_i and u(x)>=-E, E>=0, the Euclidean ball B(x,2r_i) contains V_i and is contained in W_i. Its volume v_i is independent of x. Submean gives integral_B p_i>=v_i p_i(x)>=-E v_i. Since u<=0,
 integral_{V_i}(-u)dmu<=M_i integral_B(-u)dLebesgue<=M_i v_i(H_i+E).
Denote this fixed affine bound by F_i(E).

Start at a point where u>-1. If its chart is V_i, the negative integral there is <=F_i(1). For an edge i–k, let m_ik=mu(V_i intersect V_k)>0. If the negative integral on V_i is <=L_i, some point of the overlap satisfies u>=-(L_i+1)/m_ik; otherwise its negative integral would exceed L_i. Apply the submean estimate in V_k to obtain L_k<=F_k((L_i+1)/m_ik). Propagate along a finite spanning tree and maximize over the finitely many possible initial vertices. This bounds every chart integral uniformly, hence ||u||_L1(mu)<=sum_i L_i.

For a sequence u_j, these bounds make u_j+rho_i L1_loc-bounded psh on W_i. By n1, extract a subsequence converging locally in L1 on every chart to psh representatives p_i. The differences p_i-rho_i agree almost everywhere on overlaps. They agree pointwise as canonical representatives: radial convolution recovers each representative from the same distribution, and convolution of the smooth corrections tends pointwise to those corrections. Thus they glue to a genuine global quasi-psh u. The finite inner cover gives global L1(mu) convergence. Distributional differentiation preserves dd^c u>=-lambda omega. The inequality u<=0 holds almost everywhere, and canonical submean recovery makes it hold everywhere.

Normalization is also preserved. Choose maximizers x_j with u_j(x_j)=0 and pass to x_j->x. In a coordinate neighborhood of x with correction rho, for each sufficiently small fixed r,
 rho(x_j)<=average_{B(x_j,r)}(u_j+rho).
L1 convergence and continuity of integration of a fixed L1 function over moving balls give rho(x)<=average_{B(x,r)}(u+rho). Let r decrease to zero. Canonical psh ball-average recovery gives u(x)>=0. Together with u<=0, this yields sup_X u=0.

If one starts with a global distribution q satisfying dd^c q>=-lambda omega, local quadratic corrections and n1 first produce canonical psh representatives q+rho_i. Their differences glue by the same recovery argument. Their global quasi-psh representative has finite supremum and can be normalized before applying the preceding proof.

This establishes actual canonical compactness and a nontrivial normalized limit. It requires neither closedness of omega nor almost-everywhere modifications. It is a mathematical argument from the stated foundations, not a computational observation.

notes.summary: Target A holds: bounded concentration pairings against ALL normalized smooth positive dd^c-closed complementary tests force a global analytic hypersurface containing U'×{0}. Consequently C_delta tends to infinity on a hypersurface-free X.
notes.detailedSummary: Lamari applied to lambda omega-B_delta gives distributions with one uniform Hessian lower bound. n2 produces genuine normalized canonical potentials and an L1 limit. Full-variable smooth testing establishes B_delta->chi[H] and lambda omega+dd^c q>=chi[H]. Local quadratic corrections yield CLOSED positive currents whose Lelong numbers agree on overlaps. Siu gives a proper global analytic upperlevel set; its codimension-one components contain the entire patch. No singular fiber restriction or nonclosed Siu application occurs.
notes.text:
We prove A with exactly its cutoff family and all its tests. Write H={zeta=0} in the chosen chart. Extend chi[H] by zero; its support is compactly contained in the chart. It is not asserted to be globally closed.

By n1, a smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed complementary form exists and can be normalized by its positive degree against omega. Thus T_omega is nonempty. For fixed delta, smoothness, compactness, and positivity of omega give 0<=B_delta<=k_delta omega with finite k_delta. Therefore 0<=C_delta<=k_delta<infinity.

Suppose delta_j decreases to zero and C_delta_j<=M. Put lambda=M+1. For any smooth strictly positive dd^c-closed complementary form Theta, its degree d_Theta=integral omega Theta is positive, and its normalization belongs to T_omega. Hence
 integral (lambda omega-B_delta_j) Theta>=(lambda-M)d_Theta>0.
Lamari's lemma in n1 applies without requiring the smooth form lambda omega-B_delta_j to be closed. It gives a real distribution q_j with
 lambda omega+dd^c q_j>=B_delta_j.
By n2 choose its genuine global quasi-psh representative and subtract its supremum. Thus sup_X q_j=0 and dd^c q_j>=-lambda omega, with the same lambda for every j. After extraction, n2 gives global L1 convergence to a genuine normalized q.

For every smooth full-variable complementary test Xi,
 integral B_delta Xi=integral_C p(xi)sigma_xi integral_z chi(z)i_{delta xi}^*Xi
 tends to integral_z chi(z)i_0^*Xi=<chi[H],Xi>,
where i_s(z)=(z,s). Compact support gives uniform convergence of the smooth coefficients. Components containing d zeta or d bar zeta are annihilated by sigma_zeta; the remaining tangential coefficients retain their full zeta dependence before taking the limit. Only smooth test forms are pulled back. No singular current is restricted to a fiber.

Consequently B_delta converges as a current to chi[H]. L1 convergence gives distributional convergence of dd^c q_j. Testing with arbitrary smooth semipositive complementary forms preserves positivity and yields
 Q:=lambda omega+dd^c q>=chi[H].
Q is generally nonclosed, since dQ=lambda d omega.

On each coordinate ball choose a smooth quadratic rho_i with dd^c rho_i>=lambda omega. Then
 S_i:=dd^c(q+rho_i)=Q+(dd^c rho_i-lambda omega)
is CLOSED and positive. On overlaps S_i-S_k=dd^c(rho_i-rho_k) is smooth. A smooth (1,1) current contributes O(r^{2n}) to its flat complementary mass in a radius-r ball; the Lelong denominator is r^{2n-2}. Its normalized contribution is therefore O(r^2), proving invariance under smooth differences. With coordinate invariance from n1, nu(x):=nu(S_i,x) is globally well defined.

Apply Siu only to the closed positive S_i, of bidimension (n-1,n-1). The local sets {nu(S_i,x)>=1} are analytic of dimension <=n-1 and agree on overlaps. They define a global closed analytic subset E. The dimension bound makes E proper.

Near any point of U'×{0}, chi=1, so S_i>=[H]. Both currents are closed there, and their difference is positive. Geometric Lelong numbers respect this inequality by their defining nonnegative ball integrals. The hyperplane normalization follows directly: with sigma=dd^c|Z|^2=i sum dZ_k wedge dbar Z_k/(2pi),
 integral_{H intersect B(0,r)} sigma^{n-1}=r^{2n-2}.
Thus nu([H],x)=1 and U'×{0} is contained in E.

Let D be the union of the global irreducible components of E having dimension n-1. The analytic-component premise checked at Demailly II.5.3 in n1 gives local finiteness; compactness makes this a finite family. Its union is a closed analytic hypersurface. At every point of the patch, the smooth irreducible (n-1)-dimensional hyperplane germ lies in E and therefore in an (n-1)-dimensional component. Components of smaller dimension cannot contain that germ. Hence D contains the whole U'×{0}.

If X has no analytic hypersurfaces and C_delta failed to tend to infinity, some finite M would bound C_delta at arbitrarily small delta. Choosing a decreasing sequence would give the forbidden D. Therefore C_delta tends to infinity.

This proves A, including global normalization, canonical compactness, full-variable current convergence, gluing, and properness. It assumes neither closedness nor balancedness of omega. It supplies no determinant estimate or admissible mass-collapse sequence.

notes.summary: Target B holds with actual global smooth logarithmic regularizations and a uniform bound C_delta<=4||p||_infinity K for sufficiently small delta, under its precise whole-chart Cartier hypothesis.
notes.detailedSummary: Modify a smooth metric on O(D) to make |s|_h^2=|zeta|^2 near every small-delta cutoff support. The globally smooth functions F_epsilon=log(|s|_h^2+epsilon^2) have a uniform Hessian lower bound. Their explicit flat-chart Hessian dominates B_delta. Smooth dd^c Stokes against every normalized complementary test gives the uniform bound. The construction permits other branches elsewhere but requires the specified simple branch throughout the cutoff support.
notes.text:
Let E=O(D) and s its canonical section. The hypothesis implies that e=s/zeta is a nowhere-zero holomorphic frame on the cutoff chart: the branch zeta=0 is simple and there are no other zeros there.

Choose delta_0 so that K_0=supp(chi)×{|zeta|<=delta_0} is compactly contained in this frame domain. Start with any global smooth Hermitian metric h_0. Put ell=log|e|_{h_0}^2 and choose a smooth cutoff alpha equal to one near K_0 and compactly supported in the frame domain. Define
 h=h_0 exp(-alpha ell),
extending alpha ell by zero. This is a global smooth positive metric with |e|_h^2=1 near K_0. Hence r:=|s|_h^2=|zeta|^2 on a fixed neighborhood of every B_delta support for delta<=delta_0.

The functions F_epsilon=log(r+epsilon^2) are globally smooth for every epsilon>0. In a local frame with squared metric exp(-phi), off D one has dd^c log r=-kappa, where kappa=dd^c phi is the global smooth curvature. The exact chain rule gives
 dd^c F_epsilon=-[r/(r+epsilon^2)]kappa+[epsilon^2 r/(r+epsilon^2)^2]d log r wedge d^c log r.
The second term is semipositive. Choose K>=1 with -K omega<=kappa<=K omega. Since r/(r+epsilon^2) lies in [0,1], dd^c F_epsilon>=-K omega off D. Smoothness extends the inequality to every point of D, including intersections of branches outside the prescribed chart.

On the fixed flat neighborhood,
 dd^c F_delta=[delta^2/(|zeta|^2+delta^2)^2]sigma_zeta.
For |zeta|<=delta this coefficient is >=1/(4delta^2). Set L=4||p||_infinity. Using chi<=1 and the support condition on p gives B_delta<=L dd^c F_delta on its support. Outside that support B_delta=0 and dd^c F_delta+K omega>=0. Therefore globally
 B_delta<=L(dd^c F_delta+K omega).

For every Theta in T_omega, smooth integration by parts on compact X gives
 integral dd^c F_delta Theta=integral F_delta dd^c Theta=0.
No d-closedness of Theta is required. Wedge the global inequality with Theta and use its normalization to obtain
 integral B_delta Theta<=LK.
Taking the supremum proves C_delta<=4||p||_infinity K uniformly for delta<=delta_0.

This uses actual global smooth logarithmic regularizations and covers all smooth tests. It gives no corresponding bound merely from an unrelated divisor or from an unspecified chart crossing branch intersections.

The exact Hessian coefficients were independently checked by verify_algebra.py. algebra_output.txt records delta^2/(delta^2+s)^2, its rescaled coefficient (1+y)^(-2), and the global profile derivatives r/(epsilon^2+r) and epsilon^2 r/(epsilon^2+r)^2. Rerun: python verify_algebra.py > algebra_output.txt. These symbolic checks verify formulas; the global metric construction and Stokes argument supply the proof. Test nonemptiness is imported from n1.

notes.summary: Target C holds exactly for its displayed radial family: positivity requires a,g>0, closure forces constant a, and the asserted root, integrals, sharp bound, and mean-only equality condition are correct.
notes.detailedSummary: The supplied surface geometry gives dd^c(g beta)=-g' c beta-g c^2 and dd^c Gamma=a'' eta^2 beta; periodicity forces constant a. An adapted coframe proves strict positivity and the unique positive square root. Fiber integration gives D=TA(a+gbar) and R=(3/2)TA sqrt(a)gbar. The bound follows from the exact factorization (a+b)^3-(27/4)ab^2=(b-2a)^2(b+a/4). Positive Fejer profiles attain equality with fixed mean and unbounded peaks. This classifies only the stated family.
notes.text:
Suppress pullbacks in the original primitive elliptic bundle. Local lifts of t differ by integer multiples of T, so dt, d^c t, beta, and smooth periodic coefficient functions descend. Use c=dd^c t, d eta=d c=0, eta c=0, and horizontality over the complex surface.

With beta=dt wedge d^c t,
 beta=i partial t wedge barpartial t/(2pi), beta^2=0,
 d beta=-dt wedge c, d^c beta=-c wedge d^c t, dd^c beta=-c^2.
Since d^c(g beta)=-g c wedge d^c t,
 dd^c(g beta)=-g' c beta-g c^2.
Multiplication by eta kills the first term by primitiveness and the second by horizontal degree. Also
 dd^c(a eta^2)=(a'' beta+a' c)eta^2=a'' eta^2 beta.
Thus dd^c Gamma=a'' eta^2 beta. This top form is everywhere positive. Closure forces a''=0, and periodicity makes a constant. Conversely constant a gives closure for every periodic g.

Choose an adapted coframe with positive rank-one forms E_1,E_2,E_3 satisfying eta=E_1+E_2 and beta=E_3. Then
 Gamma=2a E_1 E_2+g E_1 E_3+g E_2 E_3.
Its complementary Hermitian matrix is diagonal with coefficients 2a,g,g, so strict positivity is equivalent to a>0 and g>0. Combining this with closure gives exactly a positive constant a and positive periodic g.

Set x=sqrt(a) and y=g/(2sqrt(a)). The genuine positive form gamma=x eta+y beta satisfies gamma^2=Gamma. It is the unique positive square root: the complementary matrix of the square of a positive Hermitian matrix H is twice its cofactor matrix, which determines H uniquely. Here this forces diagonal entries x,x,y.

On a fiber, t=2 log|w| up to a base-dependent shift, and d^c t=d theta/(2pi). Therefore integral_fiber beta=T, and for periodic h,
 integral_X h(t)eta^2 beta=A integral_0^T h(t)dt=TA hbar.
The interval shift is immaterial by periodicity. Since eta^3=0 and beta^2=0,
 omega Gamma=(a+g)eta^2 beta,
 gamma^3=(3/2)sqrt(a)g eta^2 beta.
With b=gbar and K=TA this yields D=K(a+b), R=(3/2)K sqrt(a)b, V=3K.

The sharp inequality is equivalent to
 (a+b)^3-(27/4)ab^2>=0.
Exactly,
 (a+b)^3-(27/4)ab^2=(b-2a)^2(b+a/4).
Hence R<=D^(3/2)/sqrt(V), with equality precisely b=2a. For D=1, the sharp parameters are a=1/(3TA), b=2/(3TA), giving R=1/sqrt(V). Pointwise constancy of g is unnecessary.

An explicit smooth equality family is
 F_N(theta)=(1/N)|sum_{k=0}^{N-1}exp(i k theta)|^2
 =1+2 sum_{k=1}^{N-1}(1-k/N)cos(k theta),
 g_N(t)=a[1+F_N(2pi t/T)], a=1/(3TA).
For N>=2, F_N is smooth, nonnegative, has mean one and peak N. Thus g_N>=a>0, gbar_N=2a, and max g_N=a(N+1) tends to infinity, while D=1 and R=1/sqrt(V) for every N. Away from t=0 modulo T, the sine-quotient formula gives F_N=O(1/N), so its peaks concentrate. These are complementary tests, not admissible Monge–Ampère potentials.

verify_algebra.py independently checks the exterior identities, the positive-root expansion, both integral coefficients, and the polynomial factorization. Its finite Fejer checks N=2,8,32,128 give mean g_N/a=2 and peaks 3,9,33,129. The analytical formulas above prove the all-N statements. algebra_output.txt records Python 3.12.14, SymPy 1.14.0, and successful exact checks. Rerun: python verify_algebra.py > algebra_output.txt. Execution does not certify the mathematical proof.

Only Gamma=a eta^2+g eta beta is classified. Arbitrary complementary tests are not replaced by this family.

Its concentration pairings diverge, but no positive-root volume divergence has been established. C controls only its radial family. A positive-matrix example explains why linear concentration alone supplies no determinant lower bound, without claiming realization by global tests. notes.text:
This last note claims complete resolution of the DECLARED RESTRICTED A–D ASSIGNMENT, using n3, n4, and n5 and their support notes. It does not claim completion of unchanged original P11.

A is reconstructed in n3, including all full-variable smooth tests, normalized canonical compactness, the current limit, locally CLOSED positive currents, and a proper globally glued analytic upperlevel set whose hypersurface part contains the whole patch. B is reconstructed in n4 with a global Cartier metric, actual smooth logarithmic regularizations, a uniform Hessian lower bound, and all-test smooth Stokes. C is reconstructed in n5 with necessity, actual positivity, the unique positive root, exact integrals, the sharp bound, and equality determined solely by gbar=2a. None of A–C is rejected.

For D, original P11 explicitly stipulates that the K3 total space has no divisors. An analytic hypersurface on a smooth complex manifold gives a divisor, so this input rules out A's hypersurface conclusion. Its X is connected and compact of complex dimension three, and omega is smooth positive. A therefore applies and gives, for every stated cutoff family,
 C_delta=sup_{Theta in T_omega} integral_X B_delta Theta -> infinity.
This uses the given no-divisor hypothesis; it is not a newly proved classification of elliptic-bundle divisors. Smooth tests approximating each finite supremum exist by its definition, but their positive-root volumes have not been estimated.

Linear pairing divergence alone supplies no determinant lower bound. Pointwise in dimension three, a positive complementary matrix Q_N=diag(N,N^(-1),N^(-1)) has trace tending to infinity and determinant tending to zero. In the convention Q=2 cof(H) for gamma^2, det H=sqrt(det Q/8), and gamma^3 is proportional to det H. This explains the missing type of estimate. It is not asserted that these matrices realize global dd^c-closed normalized tests.

C's bound covers only Gamma=a eta^2+g eta beta. Its smooth degree-one equality family has arbitrarily high peaks with constant root integral, and C supplies no estimate on other tests. A does not enlarge that classified family, and B requires the exact local divisor branch. Neither an all-test root-volume theorem nor an all-potential lower-mass theorem has been established.

No genuine smooth admissible mass-collapse sequence is constructed here. No exact K3 v_minus, positive K3 lower bound, or proof or counterexample to universal vanishing for nonzero real Chern class is supplied. The original completion criteria remain open. Restricted completion must not be interpreted as original completion.

The complete saved deliverable is restricted_notes.json, with individual proof texts notes/n1.md through notes/n6.md. Input is in assignment_input.json. The implementation and exact output are verify_algebra.py and algebra_output.txt.
